title.narrative: Integrated lifesaving RH and GBV services to the most vulnerable women and girls in the priority districts under the CERF allocation in Yemen, 2024-2025.

description.narrative: Yemen's ongoing humanitarian crisis has had a devastating impact on women and girls, exacerbating gender inequalities, increasing their vulnerability to gender-based violence, and limiting their access to essential reproductive health services, often with life-threatening consequences. According to the 2024 HNO, 18.2 million people—over 55 per cent of the population—will need humanitarian assistance and protection services in Yemen. Additionally, in 2024, approximately 17.8 million individuals in Yemen required health assistance, including 3.2 million IDPs. A total of 24 percent of people in need are women, who require access to various medical and reproductive healthcare services, including 4 per cent pregnant women in need of emergency obstetric care. Yemen’s Poly crisis that also includes climate-induced disasters, currency depreciation, limited income opportunities, rising costs of basic commodities, challenges faced by aid agencies, bureaucratic restrictions on female staff, the detention of aid workers in northern Yemen, and the regional escalation of hostilities impacting the Hodeidah port, which supplies 80% of humanitarian assistance to northern Yemen, have further created protection risks, as well as compromised access to life-saving RH services. In response to the escalating humanitarian crisis and its impact on women and girls, UNFPA with funding support from the CERF proposes an integrated one-year project aiming to provide a comprehensive RH and GBV response to the most vulnerable women and girls in underserved districts. Additionally, the integrated project will prioritize "essential lifesaving and life-sustaining activities". Some of the activities will be implemented through forming case-management WG in some selected areas.The CERF will serve two key purposes: as seed money to initiate lifesaving interventions and to scale up existing interventions in others project sites. This will significantly strengthen lifesaving programs through the establishment and enhancement of Women and Girls Safe Spaces, along with bolstering supported Reproductive Health Facilities. These interventions will provide an integrated comprehensive response that is aimed at providing RH and GBV services, both stand-alone activities and integrated, recognizing the strong interconnection between these aspects as essential components in effectively meeting the health and protection needs of women and girls affected by emergencies.The support provided through this funding is set to play a vital role in delivering essential services to some of the most vulnerable populations, with a particular emphasis on women, girls, and IDPs who find themselves residing in informal settings as well as within host communities that were recently affected by the floods. The focus will be directed towards key areas such as multisectoral GBV response, reproductive health care, Mental Health, and MHPSS, in addition to a range of protection and referral services through the support of CVA targeting 1,000 women and girls under GBV and 1,000 under the RH services.A total of 102,385 women and girls will benefit from this fund, with 53,572, receiving essential and life-saving reproductive health services and 48,813 receiving GBV support. Additionally, approximately 12,000 men and boys will indirectly benefit through awareness-raising activities and support for women and girls with delivery complications. CVA will be used as facilitation modality to ensure improved access to RH- GBV integrated servicesThe project will operate in 6 Governorates and 9 districts: Hodieda:Az Zuhra - WGSS + RH supplies (Zuhra hospital), Al Luhaya - referrals + CEmONC (Alluhaya hospital)Hajjah: Abs - WGSS + BEmONC (Robo Matwala HC), Aslam – WGSS + BEmONC (Bani-Zaid Aslm), Mustaba - WGSS+ BEmONC (Al Khames HC)Marib: Marib AlWadi - WGSS + CEmONC (Kara hospital)Lahj: Tuban - WGSS +CVATaizz: AlMakha – GBV and RH referrals +CVA Amanat AlAsimah: Bani AlHarith – referrals +BEmONC (Bait Handal)
